newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Simsmetal shares surge after Q3 profit.
newsitem.headline: Simsmetal shares surge after Q3 profit.

text.p: Shares in metals recycler Simsmetal Ltd surged over 2.5 percent to A$8.15 on Tuesday after it announced a third quarter net profit of A$7.99 million.

This represented a 38 percent increase on the second quarter, the company said. The stronger third quarter result followed forecasts by the company of improved profitability in the second half as trading conditions improved.
Chief executive officer John Crabb forecast a further improvement in results providing there was no deterioration in trading conditions.

Commenting on the results, Crabb said all regions had shown improved earnings in the third quarter. "Most operations in Australia and overseas performed at above forecast levels, with improvements in profitability recorded over the second quarter of the 1997 financial year in all operating regions."
Brokers said investors had been attracted by the improved result and were optimistic about the last quarter's performance.
"They called it higher and have delivered so far," said a Sydney broker, adding that the stronger outlook was encouraging.
"It looks promising for the full year figure."
By 3.30 p.m. (0530 GMT), Simsmetal shares had pushed further ahead, reaching a record high A$8.24, up 3.6 percent on the day, on solid turnover of 355,225 shares.
